It is always possible to choose a path
\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow{\cal C}_{\mathsf{Hilb}_{f}}^{\vee}(\mathbf{1},A)
, such that
\gamma(0)=\iota
and
\gamma(1)=p
.
Then
{\cal L}\circ\gamma
is a path of the commuting models, with
{\cal L}\circ\gamma(0)={\cal L}_{\iota}=\left(\mathbb{Z},{\mathsf{H}},A,-m^{\dagger}m\right)
be the original model and
{\cal L}\circ\gamma(1)={\cal L}_{p}=(\mathbb{Z},{\mathsf{H}},A,-m(p)^{\dagger}m(p))
be the deformed model.

Suppose
p
reduces the Q-system to
(A_{P},m_{P},\iota_{P})
(proposition
F.11
), we show that the
H
-type ground state of
{\cal L}_{p}
is one-to-one correspondence to that of
(\mathbb{Z},{\mathsf{H}},A_{P},-m_{P}^{\dagger}m_{P})
. Suppose
\omega

is an
H
-type ground state for
(\mathbb{Z},{\mathsf{H}},A,1-m(p)^{\dagger}m(p))
, then

\displaystyle\frac{|p^{\dagger}p|}{d_{A}}

\displaystyle=\omega(m^{\dagger}_{i,i+1}(p)m_{i,i+1}(p))

\displaystyle=\omega\bigg(m^{\dagger}_{i-1,i}(p)m_{i-1,i}(p)m^{\dagger}_{i,i+1}(p)m_{i,i+1}(p)\times m^{\dagger}_{i+1,i+2}(p)m_{i+1,i+2}(p)\bigg)

\displaystyle=\omega\bigg(m^{\dagger}_{i-1,i}(p)m_{i-1,i}(p)\frac{|p^{\dagger}p|}{d_{A}}m^{\dagger}_{P,i,i+1}m_{P,i,i+1}m^{\dagger}_{i+1,i+2}(p)m_{i+1,i+2}(p)\bigg)

\displaystyle=\frac{|p^{\dagger}p|}{d_{A}}\omega\left(m^{\dagger}_{P,i,i+1}m_{P,i,i+1}\right)

for any
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.
Conversely, if
\omega
is an
H
-type ground state for
(\mathbb{Z},{\mathsf{H}},A_{P},1-m_{P}^{\dagger}m_{P})
, we have

\displaystyle 1

\displaystyle=\omega(m^{\dagger}_{P,i,i+1}m_{P,i,i+1})

\displaystyle=\omega\bigg(m^{\dagger}_{P,i-1,i}m_{P,i-1,i}m^{\dagger}_{P,i,i+1}m_{P,i,i+1}m^{\dagger}_{P,i+1,i+2}m_{P,i+1,i+2}\bigg)

\displaystyle=\frac{d_{A}}{|p^{\dagger}p|}\omega\bigg(m^{\dagger}_{P,i-1,i}m_{P,i-1,i}m^{\dagger}_{i,i+1}(p)m_{i,i+1}(p)m^{\dagger}_{P,i+1,i+2}m_{P,i+1,i+2}\bigg)

\displaystyle=\frac{d_{A}}{|p^{\dagger}p|}\omega\bigg(m^{\dagger}_{i,i+1}(p)m_{i,i+1}(p)\bigg)

for any
i\in\mathbb{Z}
. Combined with Remark
5
, any Morita equivalent Q-systems realize the same phase.

Appendix H
Bimodule category
{}_{A_{+}}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}})_{A_{+}}

First, we can show a result that will be used later. For a finite group
G
and a 2-cocycle
\psi\in Z^{2}(G,U(1))
with
\psi(e,g)=\psi(g,e)=1
for any
g\in G
,

\psi(g,h)\psi(h^{-1},g^{-1})=\frac{\psi(g,g^{-1})\psi(h,h^{-1})}{\psi(gh,h^{-1}h^{-1})}.

Thus
\psi(g,h)\psi(h^{-1},g^{-1})
is cohomologously trivial.

We fix the presentation
S_{3}=\langle s,r|s^{2}=r^{3}=e,\ srs=r^{2}\rangle
and
\mathbb{Z}_{3}=\langle a|a^{3}=e\rangle
. We consider
A_{+}=\mathbb{C}^{\psi_{+}}\langle r,a\rangle\in\mathsf{Hilb}_{S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}}
, where
\psi_{+}(g,h)=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}g_{2}h_{1}}
. Following
[
107
]
, we compute the bimodule category
{}_{A_{+}}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}})_{A_{+}}
. Below, we use
1_{g}
to represent a basis of
\mathbb{C}_{g}
, such that
1_{g}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{h}=1_{gh}
. And the multiplication of
A_{+}
is defined on basis as

1_{g}\cdot 1_{h}=\psi_{+}(g,h)1_{gh}.

H.1
As a linear category

The double cosets
\langle r,a\rangle\setminus(S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3})/\langle r,a\rangle
are

\langle r,a\rangle,\quad s\langle r,a\rangle.

The groups and cocycles defined in
[
107
]
are:

•

\langle r,a\rangle^{e}=\langle r,a\rangle
:

\psi^{e}(c,d)=\psi_{+}(c,d)\psi_{+}(d^{-1},c^{-1})\sim_{\mathrm{coh}}1

which is a trivial 2-cocycle following from the result discussed above. The projective representations of
\langle r,a\rangle
with projective phase
\psi^{e}
are 1-dimensional. Thus

\left|\mathrm{Irr}\left(\mathsf{Rep}^{\psi^{e}}\langle r,a\rangle^{e}\right)\right|=9.

We choose the
1
-dimensional projective representations
\rho_{ij}:\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}\rightarrow\mathrm{PGL}(U_{ij})
of
\langle r,a\rangle^{e}
with projective phase
\psi^{e}
:

\rho_{ij}(r^{m})=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}im},\quad\rho_{ij}(a^{n})=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}jn},\quad i,\,j,\,m,\,n=0,\,1,\,2.

And we define

\rho_{ij}(r^{m}a^{n}):=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}mn}{3}}\rho_{ij}(a^{m})\rho_{ij}(r^{n})=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(im+jn-mn)}.

We denote the simple
A_{+}
-bimodule related to the projective representation
(U_{ij},\rho_{ij})
as
[ij]
.

•

\langle r,a\rangle^{s}=\langle r,a\rangle
:

\displaystyle\psi^{s}(c,d)

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(c,d)\psi_{+}(s^{-1}d^{-1}s,s^{-1}c^{-1}s)

\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(c_{2}d_{1}-c_{1}d_{2})}

\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}c_{2}d_{1}}\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}c_{1}c_{2}}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}d_{1}d_{2}}}{\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(c_{1}+d_{1})(c_{2}+d_{2})}}

\displaystyle\sim_{\mathrm{coh}}\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}c_{2}d_{1}}

which is a non-trivial 2-cocycle. The representation of
\mathbb{C}^{\psi^{s}}\langle r,a\rangle^{s}
is
3
-dimensional. Thus

\left|\mathrm{Irr}\left(\mathsf{Rep}^{\psi^{s}}\langle r,a\rangle^{s}\right)\right|=1

The
3
-dimensional projective representation
\rho_{V}:\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}\rightarrow\mathrm{PGL}(V)
of
\langle r,a\rangle^{s}
can be chosen as

\rho_{V}(r^{m})=\begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}&0&0\\
0&1&0\\
0&0&\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}\end{pmatrix}^{m},\quad\rho_{V}(a^{n})=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\
1&0&0\\
0&1&0\end{pmatrix}^{n}.

We then have

\rho_{V}(r^{m}a^{n}):=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}mn}\rho_{V}(r^{m})\rho_{V}(a^{n}),

\rho_{V}(a^{n})\rho_{V}(r^{m})=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}mn}\rho_{V}(r^{m}a^{n}),

Denote the simple bimodule related to the projective representation
(V,\rho_{V})
as
\sigma
. Since
\sigma
is the unique non-invertible object in the bimodule category with the quantum dimension
d_{\sigma}=3
, the fusion rule is Tambara-Yamagami-type. There are several groups of order
18
:

D_{18},\quad\mathbb{Z}_{9}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2},\quad S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3},\quad(\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3})\rtimes_{\varphi}\mathbb{Z}_{2},\quad\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2},

Here
\varphi_{1}(a,b)=(-a,-b)
.
None of these groups have irreducible representation of dimension-
3
. Thus the bimodule category here does not correspond to any group representation category.

From the above setup, the bimodule category is isomorphic to
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathsf{H}})
as a linear category, where
{\mathsf{H}}
is an algebra

{\mathsf{H}}=\mathbb{C}^{\psi^{e}}\langle r,a\rangle\oplus\mathbb{C}^{\psi^{s}}\langle r,a\rangle.

We denote the basis in
\mathbb{C}^{\psi^{e}}\langle r,a\rangle
as
\{g_{e}\}_{g\in\langle r,a\rangle}
, and in
\mathbb{C}^{\psi^{s}}\langle r,a\rangle
as
\{g_{s}\}_{g\in\langle r,a\rangle}
.

H.2
As a fusion category

The Tambara-Yamagami category
\mathrm{TY}_{G}^{\chi,\epsilon}
is defined by

•

an abelian group
G
and a symmetric non-degenerate bi-character
\chi:G\times G\rightarrow U(1)
;

•

the Frobenius-Schur indicator
\epsilon=\pm 1
.

Below we will determine
\chi
and
\epsilon
.

We first fix the left
A
-action “
\underset{}{\triangleright}
” and the right
A
-action “
\underset{}{\triangleleft}
”.

•

[ij]
: The invertible objects are
[ij]=U_{ij}\otimes A
, the right
A
-module action on which is given by the free
A
-multiplication, and

1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{g^{-1}}=\rho_{ij}(g)u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e},\quad\forall u_{ij}\in U_{ij}.

•

\sigma
: the non-invertible bimodule is
\sigma=V\underset{}{\otimes}s\underset{}{\otimes}A
, the right
A
-module action is given by the free
A
-multiplication and

1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(v\underset{}{\otimes}s\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}gs}=\rho_{V}(g)(v)\underset{}{\otimes}s\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e},\quad\forall v\in V.

The relative tensor product is defined as

U\underset{A}{\otimes}V:=U\underset{}{\otimes}V/\langle u\underset{}{\triangleleft}a\underset{}{\otimes}v-u\underset{}{\otimes}a\underset{}{\triangleright}v\rangle.

Thus

u\underset{}{\triangleleft}a\underset{A}{\otimes}v=u\underset{A}{\otimes}a\underset{}{\triangleright}v.

•

[ij]\underset{A}{\otimes}[kl]
: The adjoint action on
u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}\underset{A}{\otimes}u_{kl}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}
is

1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{A}{\otimes}(u_{kl}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{g^{-1}}=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}(\rho_{ij}(g)u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{A}{\otimes}(\rho_{kl}(g)u_{kl}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}).

Thus the effective action on the vector space
U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}U_{kl}
is encoded by the map

\rho_{U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}U_{kl}}(g):=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}\rho_{ij}(g)\underset{}{\otimes}\rho_{kl}(g).

•

[ij]\underset{A}{\otimes}\sigma
: The adjoint action is

\displaystyle\quad 1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{A}{\otimes}(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{g^{-1}}\underset{A}{\otimes}1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}\bigg(\rho(g)(u_{ij})\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}\bigg)\underset{A}{\otimes}\bigg(\rho_{V}(g)(v)\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg).

The effective action on the vector space
U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}V
is encoded by the map

\rho_{U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}V}(g):=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}\rho_{ij}(g)\underset{}{\otimes}\rho_{V}(g).

•

\sigma\underset{A}{\otimes}[ij]
:
The adjoint action on
v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\underset{A}{\otimes}u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}\in\sigma\underset{A}{\otimes}[ij]
is

\displaystyle\quad 1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s})\underset{A}{\otimes}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}\underset{A}{\otimes}1_{s^{-1}gs}(u_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e})\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}\bigg(\rho_{V}(g)(v)\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{A}{\otimes}\bigg(\rho_{ij}(s^{-1}gs)(u_{ij})\underset{}{\otimes}1_{e}\bigg).

We find that the effective action on the vector space
V\underset{}{\otimes}U_{ij}
is encoded by the map

\rho_{V\underset{}{\otimes}U_{ij}}(g):=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}\rho_{V}(g)\underset{}{\otimes}\rho_{ij}(s^{-1}gs).

•

\sigma\underset{}{\otimes}\sigma
: The adjoint action is

\displaystyle\quad 1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}\bigg(u\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{A}{\otimes}\bigg(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{g^{-1}}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}1_{g}\underset{}{\triangleright}\bigg(u\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{s^{-1}g^{-1}s}\underset{A}{\otimes}1_{s^{-1}gs}\underset{}{\triangleright}\bigg(v\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{}{\triangleleft}1_{g^{-1}}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}\bigg(\rho_{V}(g)(u)\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg)\underset{A}{\otimes}\bigg(\rho_{V}(s^{-1}gs)(v)\underset{}{\otimes}1_{s}\bigg).

The effective action on the vector space
V\underset{}{\otimes}V
is encoded by the map

\rho_{V\underset{}{\otimes}V}(g):=\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}\rho_{V}(g)\underset{}{\otimes}\rho_{V}(s^{-1}gs).

With the conjugation action on the relative tensor product space, we now fix the intertwiner of the fusion.

•

[(i+k)(j+l)]\rightarrow[ij]\underset{}{\otimes}[kl]
:

\displaystyle\quad\psi_{+}((r^{m}a^{n})^{-1},r^{m}a^{n})^{-1}\rho_{ij}(r^{m}a^{n})\rho_{kl}(r^{m}a^{n})

\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}mn}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(im+jn-mn)}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(km+ln-mn)}

\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}((i+k)m+(j+l)n-mn)}

\displaystyle=\rho_{i+k,j+l}(r^{m}a^{n}).

Thus the abelian group
G
of the Tambara-Yamagami category is
\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}
;

•

\sigma\rightarrow[ij]\underset{}{\otimes}\sigma
: the bimodule map condition implies that we only need to find the intertwiner
f_{ij}:V\rightarrow U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}V
, that is, a linear map
f_{ij}
such that

\rho_{U_{ij}\underset{}{\otimes}V}(g)f_{ij}=f_{ij}\rho_{V}(g),\quad\forall g\in\langle r,a\rangle.

We find

f_{10}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\
0&0&1\\
1&0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad f_{01}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}&0&0\\
0&1&0\\
0&0&\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}\end{pmatrix}.

•

\sigma\rightarrow\sigma\underset{}{\otimes}[ij]
: we need to determine the intertwiner
k_{ij}:V\rightarrow V\underset{}{\otimes}U_{ij}

\rho_{V\underset{}{\otimes}U_{ij}}(g)f_{ij}=f_{ij}\rho_{V}(g),\quad\forall g\in\langle r,a\rangle.

We find

k_{10}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\
1&0&0\\
0&1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad k_{01}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}&0&0\\
0&1&0\\
0&0&\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i}/3}\end{pmatrix}.

•

[ij]\rightarrow\sigma\underset{}{\otimes}\sigma
:
we find the intertwiner
m_{ij}:U_{ij}\rightarrow V\underset{}{\otimes}V
, such that

\rho_{V\underset{}{\otimes}V}(g)m_{ij}=m_{ij}\rho_{ij}(g).

Now we compute the bi-character with the intertwiners. First, it is easy to see that

\chi(r,r)=\chi(a,a)=1.

Since

f_{10}k_{01}=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}}k_{01}f_{10},

we have

\chi(r,a)=\chi(a,r)=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}}.

Thus, the bicharacter is

\chi(g,h)=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}(g_{1}h_{2}+g_{2}h_{1})}.

And since the
m_{00}
coincides with the coevaluation map, the Frobenius-Schur indicator
\epsilon=1
.

We have the result:

{}_{A_{+}}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{S_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}})_{A_{+}}\cong\mathrm{TY}_{\mathbb{Z}_{3}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3}}^{\chi,\epsilon},\quad\chi(g,h)=\exp{\left[\frac{2\pi\mathrm{i}}{3}\left(g_{1}h_{2}+g_{2}h_{1}\right)\right]},\quad\epsilon=1.

The fusion structure gives
{\mathsf{H}}
a Hopf algebra structure, which can be directly read off from above

\displaystyle\mathbf{1}

\displaystyle=e_{e}+e_{s},

\displaystyle\Delta g_{e}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}g_{e}\underset{}{\otimes}g_{e}+\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}g_{s}\underset{}{\otimes}s^{-1}g_{s}s,

\displaystyle\Delta g_{s}

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g)^{-1}g_{e}\underset{}{\otimes}g_{s}+\psi_{+}(s^{-1}g^{-1}s,s^{-1}gs)^{-1}g_{s}\underset{}{\otimes}s^{-1}g_{e}s,

\displaystyle\epsilon(g_{e})

\displaystyle=\psi_{+}(g^{-1},g),\quad\epsilon(g_{s})=0,

\displaystyle S(g_{e})

\displaystyle=g_{e}^{-1},\quad S(g_{s})=s^{-1}g_{s}^{-1}s.
